observations: Photo 0: PS4 console (fat body style, two-tone matte/glossy top) with two DualShock 4 controllers resting on top, a power cable, and a folded paper/receipt taped around one controller's cable.
Photo 1: Top-down view confirming the 'PS4' / PlayStation logo molded into the corner of the console, dust visible on the case, same paper tag taped to the black controller's cable.
Photo 2: Side/front view showing the console's disc-slot edge, the power brick/cable, and a second controller with heavy custom paint (blue/red/teal splatter) showing chips and wear on the shell.
No photo shows the console powered on, no home screen, no system menu, no firmware/jailbreak tool screen.
No photo shows the rear label or bottom sticker that states storage capacity or model/serial number.
No HDMI cable is visible in any photo, only the power cord/brick.
One controller shell is visibly damaged/worn (paint chipping, discoloration), the other looks stock but of unknown condition (sticks, triggers not tested).

read_from: photo 1 PS4 logo and two-tone body shape typical of the original 'Fat' PS4

claims.evidence: No photo shows the rear/bottom label that states storage capacity; body shape in photo 0/1 is consistent with a Fat PS4 but capacity cannot be confirmed from any image.
No screenshot of system menu, firmware version, or jailbreak tool is shown in any photo; this claim cannot be checked from stills.
No power-on photo or video is provided; console and controllers are shown off and static only.
Photo 2 shows one controller with visible paint chipping and wear, and photo 0/1 show dust on the console body, inconsistent with a clean 'good condition' claim for the controller at least.

risks.risk: Console may not power on or may have a dead Blu-ray drive/HDD, common in older used PS4 units
risks.proof: A video clip of the console being powered on to the home screen and a disc being read

risks.risk: Storage capacity may differ from claimed 500GB (could be 500GB, 1TB, or a swapped smaller drive)
risks.proof: Photo of the rear/bottom label showing model number and storage capacity
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common capacity (500GB) as a worst case, not higher

risks.risk: 'Hacked' firmware may be unstable, unsupported, or could brick on update attempts, and modified consoles often cannot use PSN or legitimate game updates
risks.proof: Screenshot of system settings showing firmware version and the jailbreak/CFW tool interface
risks.if_unproven: priced as a stock, unmodified console with no added value for the 'hack', and flagged as added resale risk

risks.risk: Custom-painted controller may have internal wear (stick drift, failing buttons) hidden by the paint job
risks.proof: Video showing analog stick movement and button presses in a game or controller test screen
risks.if_unproven: priced as a controller with stick drift / functional defect

risks.risk: No HDMI cable included, which is needed to use the console
risks.proof: Photo showing an HDMI cable included with the bundle
risks.if_unproven: priced as HDMI cable not included, buyer must source separately

risks.risk: Unexplained paper tag taped to one controller's cable, origin/purpose unclear
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the paper tag showing what it says
risks.if_unproven: treated as cosmetic/irrelevant, no price impact, but flagged as unverifiable detail

proof_requests: Video of the console powered on to the PS4 home screen, then loading a disc or digital game
Clear photo of the rear/bottom label showing model number and storage capacity
Screenshot of System > System Information showing firmware version, or the jailbreak/CFW tool screen, to support the 'hacked' claim
Video of both controllers' analog sticks and all buttons being pressed in a controller test app
Photo confirming an HDMI cable is included in the sale
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a used Sony PlayStation 4 (Fat) bundle with two controllers, but every seller claim (capacity, 'hacked' status, 'fully working') is unverifiable from stills alone, and visible wear on one controller contradicts the 'good condition' claim, so it must be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly modified console with a defective controller and no confirmed HDMI cable.
